summary: Onboarding: near-real-time audit socket (WS) with per-event signed envelopes, out-of-order reassembly, and clock-drift canonicalization
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a near-real-time WebSocket audit sink (persistent connection) for streaming activity events into their SIEM. Requirements: per-event signed envelope (customer-provided ed25519 keypair), deterministic UTC canonicalization of event timestamps, out-of-order reassembly with sequence-window acknowledgements, and a clock-drift report attached to daily manifests. Customer also needs a sample mapping of fields to their Splunk/QRadar schema and a short runbook for replaying missed ranges.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete SIEM onboarding for critical security telemetry; currently relying on hourly S3 dumps which delay detection (compliance gap).
- Regulatory timeline: onboarding due for an internal audit in two weeks.

Customer environment and details:
- Account: VANG-ACCT-17
- Tier: Enterprise with Dedicated support
- Typical event volume: ~3k events/sec during peak (authentication + audit trail events)
- Desired sink: persistent WebSocket with optional TLS client auth and per-event signature validation on their side
- Required proof elements: per-day clock-drift report (max skew), evidence of deterministic timestamp canonicalization (ISO8601 UTC), and an example replay token workflow for range re-ingest
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer attempted to connect via our existing streaming audit WebSocket endpoint using their integration token and a test client on 2026-03-09
2) They received an intermittent disconnect after ~6 minutes with no resume token returned
3) Several events appeared out-of-order on their side due to batching windows; they could not validate order because messages arrived without a signed envelope format they expected
4) Customer tried downloading the hourly S3 archive for the same period and saw timestamps in local timezone (Europe/Amsterdam) while their processing expects UTC canonicalization
logs: 2026-03-09T14:18:12Z ws-proxy[conn=xyz] WARN: connection terminated idle_timeout=360s reason=client-closed
2026-03-09T14:18:13Z audit-export batch[window=160ms] DEBUG: emitted 320 events seq_start=110987 seq_end=111306 timezone=Europe/Amsterdam
2026-03-09T14:18:13Z audit-export signer WARN: no-envelope-key-configured account=VANG-ACCT-17 returning unsigned-payload
comments: 2026-03-10 - Elena Korsakov (Customer): We need per-event signature so our SIEM can verify provenance. Hourly S3 is not acceptable for incident response. ETA for compliance audit is 2026-03-24.
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Collecting logs and escalation to SRE/Export team. Assigned to Carlos.

2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (SRE): Noted ws-proxy idle timeout default is 6 minutes. For enterprise customers we can enable keepalive and resume tokens, but per-event signing is an export-layer feature. Reproduced disconnects in staging with high heartbeat jitter.

2026-03-11 - Tom Beckett (Eng - Export): Hypothesis: signing code path disabled when customer hasn't uploaded key. Also timestamp canonicalization happens post-export mapping; timezone info preserved in archive which caused non-UTC timestamps in S3. Proposed short-term: enable signed-envelope shim on proxy and provide signed sample; long-term: add ed25519 per-event signatures in export pipeline.

2026-03-12 - Support (Carlos Rivera): Shared workaround with customer: temporary enablement of persistent S3 delta with HMAC manifest and 1-minute publish window; we will run a scoped implementation of per-event signed wrapper as a toggle for their account while engineering builds full feature. Customer asked for a replay runbook and a sample Splunk mapping; attaching below.
investigation_notes: SRE reproduced disconnects caused by ws-proxy idle timeout and lack of periodic ping from client lib (their client used an old ws lib). Implemented keepalive config change on a single staging node and observed stable connection >30 minutes.

Export service does not sign events per-account by default. There is code to attach a signed envelope but it is gated behind 'per_event_signing' feature flag and requires customer key in secret manager under path: secrets/audit-keys/<account>.

Timestamps in S3 archives retained original event timezone; canonicalization to UTC happens during streaming-only normalization. For compliance evidence we need to produce a manifest sample showing ISO8601 UTC conversion and a log of conversions to prove determinism.

Sequence numbers are generated per-producer shard; out-of-order arrivals stem from cross-shard reordering during multi-producer batching. Solution: include a composite sequence token (shard_id:seq) and provide a reassembly window of 60s for the SIEM sink with explicit ack semantics (timebucketed-acks).
resolution_notes:
Planned rollout and temporary mitigations:
1) Short-term (within 48 hours): Enable ws-proxy keepalive and resume-token toggle for VANG-ACCT-17; enable 1-minute delta S3 publish with an HMAC-signed manifest. Provide sample Splunk props and transforms mapping JSON and runbook for replaying ranges using resume tokens.
2) Medium-term (2 weeks): Engineering to enable per-event envelope signing behind feature flag. Implementation tasks: secret-manager integration for ed25519 keys, signer at export pipeline, composite sequence token, and clock-drift aggregation to daily manifest. PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1982.
3) Deliverables to customer: sample signed-envelope specification, signed test corpus for verification, daily clock-drift report, and replay runbook.
Follow-ups: add account-level flag to enable signed envelopes and update Confluence runbook. Owner: Tom Beckett (Export Eng).
next_steps: 1) Support to schedule configuration change for ws-proxy keepalive on prod for account VANG-ACCT-17 (Carlos)
2) Engineering to create feature branch for per-event signing and schedule canary (Tom)
3) Send signed sample corpus and Splunk mapping to customer and confirm validation (Support)
4) Prepare acceptance criteria for compliance audit (include manifest examples and clock-drift calculations)
